_comment: Editorial blips for snapshot pages. Keyed by SLUG (listings.js baseSlug output), NOT url -- url collides on multi-service vendors. Owned by Claude (Web); content Sean-approved 2026-07-26 (snapshot-blips thread). Rendered at build time by [slug].astro; a missing key renders nothing. This file is NOT touched by generate_editorial.py -- do not move the merge into the generator (it rebuilds rows from a fixed key set and would drop the field).
token-risk: When an agent needs to size up an ERC-20 or a wallet before it interacts, token-risk hands back a structural read — a 0–100 safety score plus the specific control powers a contract holds, like mint, pause, or blacklist, flagged no matter who the issuer is. It's structure, not reputation. Two endpoints, a cent each, USDC on Base, no signup.
402found: If you're wiring guardrails into an agent, 402Found is a set of small MCP servers you can call one at a time — scrub PII out of text, flag a prompt-injection attempt, check whether an action sits inside an agent's permissions, catch likely hallucinations, convert a format. Eighteen tools in all, each paid per call in USDC on Base from a fifth of a cent up. Open source, and on Smithery if you'd rather install than call.
zugabot-code-agent: When an agent needs code work done and paid for by the call, Zugabot's code agent covers the everyday jobs — review a diff, fix a bug, generate tests, write docs, refactor, run a security audit, or hand it a whole repo to go through. Prices run from a quarter a call up to $5 for the full-repo pass, all in USDC on Base.
macro-pulse: Macro Pulse rolls World Bank data — GDP growth, inflation, unemployment trend — into a single momentum score your agent can pull for any country by its code. Two cents for one country, a nickel for a batch of up to eight, cached six hours. USDC on Base.
stelar-digital: If your agent's running a grid, Stelar's a corner it can lean on for live numbers — real profit-and-loss straight off a bot in production, grid parameters sized to the asset and capital you're trading, a read on the current market regime, and a sentiment score to round it out. Eight endpoints, anywhere from half a cent to $2.50 a call, all in USDC on Base.
base-tx-decision: About to fire off a Base transaction? tx-decision reads the chain live and calls it — submit now or wait — then sizes the max and priority fees (EIP-1559) and estimates the cost. A network-economics snapshot and an MCP server come with it. A cent a call, USDC on Base.
deskcrew: For an agent working a support queue, DeskCrew is a set of helpdesk tools — draft a reply grounded in a knowledge base, work a real ticket, or search the KB and list open issues, with those lookups free and needing no signup. Sixteen tools, two to eight cents for the paid ones, and a person signs off before anything reaches a customer. Base USDC, with Polygon, Avalanche, Sei, and Solana also supported.
zugabot-image-generation: Need your agent to make an image? Zugabot's generation endpoint takes a text prompt and returns a URL — FLUX Schnell at 15 cents or FLUX 2 Pro at 50, each call coming back with the dimensions and the seed. USDC on Base.
